summary_en: ROE target maintained at 10%+ for FY2026. Equity spread (ROE minus 7–8% cost of capital) to be recovered. FY2025 ROE fell to 7.8% due to lower order volumes and reduced large-scale maintenance contracts; PBR remains above 1.0x despite 3.4% stock decline YoY. Focus on business recovery and capital efficiency in next medium-term plan (FY2027–2031).
title_en: Response to Capital Cost and Stock Price-Conscious Management for FY2026
translation_en_brief: Miyaji Engineering Group announced on 6 August 2026 a capital-cost-focused operating target for FY2026. The company acknowledges that FY2025 performance fell short: ROE declined to 7.8%, failing to exceed the 7–8% cost of equity, and the stock price dropped 3.4% year-over-year despite PBR remaining above 1.0x. The root causes were reduced public-sector order volumes (steel tonnage in bridge projects fell from ~200,000 tonnes in FY2022 to under 100,000 tonnes in FY2025) and the absence of large-scale maintenance contracts that had supported FY2024 revenue. The company reaffirms a 10%+ ROE target for FY2026 and emphasises that recovery of the equity spread and stock price requires sustained improvement in operating performance and capital returns. The tough operating environment is expected to persist into the first half of the next medium-term plan (FY2027–2031). Management acknowledges market feedback and commits to rebuilding investor confidence through business recovery and improved capital efficiency.
